mechanism_fit: This realises M3, a split between a definer and an adapter. The definer is SaddlePointExpansion.getDeviancePart(x, mu). It returns the deviance term x*log(x/mu) + mu - x, not the plain x*log(x/mu). The "+ mu - x" makes the convention look unusual, but it is fixed in three places: a javadoc-only context edit states the formula, a new passing unit test pins it (PoissonDistributionTest::testDevianceTermValues), and a second production caller depends on it (PoissonDistribution.probability, whose pmf is checked by PoissonDistributionTest::testDensities). The adapter is SaddlePointExpansion.logBinomialProbability, which consumes the definer's value. In its boundary branches it has to remove the mu - x part. The fault drops that conversion ("- n * q") in the x == n, q < 0.1 branch, so the line still reads as complete. The trigger enters through the public BinomialDistribution.probability. Its observed value (0.95^20 * e) is what you get if either getDeviancePart has the wrong convention or the adapter skipped the conversion. Only the adapter edit fixes it without breaking the Poisson pmf.
gold: org.apache.commons.math3.distribution.SaddlePointExpansion::logBinomialProbability (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/distribution/SaddlePointExpansion.java). Fault edit: "ret = -getDeviancePart(n, n * p) - n * q;" -> "ret = -getDeviancePart(n, n * p);" in the x == n, q < 0.1 branch.

ownership_reason: getDeviancePart (the definer) returns x*log(x/mu) + mu - x. Three things fix this: its javadoc (context edit), the passing unit test PoissonDistributionTest::testDevianceTermValues, and its second production caller PoissonDistribution.probability, whose pmf exp(-stirlingError(x) - getDeviancePart(x, mean)) / sqrt(2*pi*x) is checked by PoissonDistributionTest::testDensities. So logBinomialProbability (the adapter) must remove the mu - x part in its boundary branches. The x == 0, p < 0.1 branch does this: -getDeviancePart(n, n*q) - n*p equals n*log(q), the value of the p >= 0.1 fallback. The x == n fallback returns n*log(p). In the faulty x == n, q < 0.1 branch, the variant returns -getDeviancePart(n, n*p), which equals n*log(p) + n*q, so P(X = n) is multiplied by exp(n*q). Putting back '- n * q' fixes the trigger and keeps the full suite green. The declared one-line definer edits either leave the trigger failing or make it pass while breaking the Poisson pmf and the definer's unit test (G9: absorbed=false for both). Within logBinomialProbability, getStirlingError is used only by the general branch, and the trigger's first assertion (P(X = 19)) passes, which shows that branch is correct.
trigger: org.apache.commons.math3.distribution.BinomialDistributionTest::testAllTrialsSucceedingAtHighRate. It builds BinomialDistribution(20, 0.95) and asserts probability(19) == 20*0.95^19*0.05 (general branch, passes) and probability(20) == FastMath.pow(0.95, 20) (x == n, q < 0.1 branch, fails), both with delta 1e-12. It adds the import org.apache.commons.math3.util.FastMath.

concerns:
1. The definer and the adapter are in the same file (SaddlePointExpansion.java, a package-private final class), not split across classes. The cross-file pieces are the entry point (BinomialDistribution.probability) and the second caller (PoissonDistribution.probability).
2. The gold method holds strong local evidence: the symmetric x == 0 branch still has '- n * p', and the fallback branches show the target values n*log(q) and n*log(p). This may make the instance easier than an ideal M3 probe, though it is still objectively solvable.
3. The convention is stated through a javadoc context edit plus a new unit test, because the original javadoc only said "a part of the deviance". This follows the recipe's "fixed by its javadoc and a passing unit test", but the explicit javadoc may weaken definer bias, as the earlier ocflb-v1 finding warns.
4. On the trigger path, getDeviancePart takes its series-expansion branch, so the odd-looking closed form "+ mu - x" is in the same method but not on the executed lines.
5. One entry-point workaround would absorb the binomial-only trigger: special-casing x == n inside BinomialDistribution.probability. It is not a natural decoy repair and was not declared for G9.
